title: A) Shankar Finance And ... vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors. on 5 July, 2014
content: taking over possession of the shop. The accused persons have admittedly paid an advance amount of Rs.17,15,000/­ to the complainant as per the endorsement attached with agreement dated 05.03.2013. However, as per clause 12 of the said agreement the accused company had agreed to take over possession of the shop on the condition that all amounts due and payable by them upto the date of possession is paid. Bare reading of the said clause clearly CC No. 441/13 page no. 8 /16 establishes that as per the agreement between the parties, possession was to be handed over only after receiving the due and payable amount. As per the endorsement with the agreement dated 05.03.2013, the accused persons were liable to pay Rs.5,00,000/­ on 05.04.2013 and further Rs.5,00,000/­ on 10.04.2013. Admittedly the accused persons are businessmen and it is not believable that the accused persons did not ask for return of the cheque in question from the complainant in case of the complainant not handing over possession of the shop like reasonable and prudent businessmen. The accused persons have not even put this to complainant witnesses in their cross examination. In the present case, if the contention of the accused persons is to be believed then there should have been demand for return of the cheque in question. However, no such demand has been made or no such legal notice has been issued by the accused persons. Further, the accused persons did not even issue any stop payment instructions to the bank which could support the claim that the cheque in question was not issued against any legal liability. It also shows that the accused persons had no objection against presentation of the cheque in question for encashment

title: A) Shankar Finance And ... vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors. on 5 July, 2014
content: the claim that the cheque in question was not issued against any legal liability. It also shows that the accused persons had no objection against presentation of the cheque in question for encashment. 14 It is also not stated anywhere in the agreement dated 05.03.2013 that the accused shall not make any further payment apart from the advance amount already paid till the complainant company completes the construction of the Mall or obtains documents like Fire NOC / completion certificate or is ready to handover possession of the shop. Therefore, the defense taken by the accused that they were not liable to pay any money to the complainant on account of the complainant not handing over possession of the shop is without any merit. 15 It is true that for offence U/s 138 NI Act the accused is not expected to CC No. 441/13 page no. 9 /16 prove his defense beyond reasonable doubt in order to rebut the statutory presumption. However, in the instant case the agreement dated 05.03.2013 is supporting the case of the complainant and no where does it say that the accused would be liable to make payment to the complainant company only after taking over possession of the shop. The accused persons were required to lead defense evidence in order to rebut the statutory presumption of the legal liability / debt arising in favour of the complainant, however, the accused persons chose not to lead any evidence and therefore in absence of the same, accused persons have failed to rebut the statutory presumption. Hence, it stands proved that the cheque in question was issued by the accused persons in discharge of legal liability / debt

title: A) Shankar Finance And ... vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors. on 5 July, 2014
content: the same, accused persons have failed to rebut the statutory presumption. Hence, it stands proved that the cheque in question was issued by the accused persons in discharge of legal liability / debt. 16 The second disputed question that arises for consideration is whether the accused persons had made any payment to the complainant within 15 days of receiving legal demand notice. In the notice framed U/s 251 Cr. PC, the accused persons have stated that they have paid the amount of Rs.1,00,000/­ by way of RTGS on 29.05.2013 after receiving the legal notice. The accused persons have also placed on record copy of accounts statement from 03.05.2013 to 13.06.2013 showing transfer of Rs.1,00,000/­ by way of RTGS dated 29.05.2013. In reply to application U/s 145(2) NI Act, the complainant has admitted the deposit of the said amount, however, the complainant has stated that the said Rs.1,00,000/­ was deposited against other dues owed by the accused persons and not against the cheque in question. 17 It is well settled law that the cause of action arises U/s 138 NI Act only when legal demand notice has been served upon the accused and that the accused failed to pay the cheque amount within 15 days of receipt of the legal notice. The CC No. 441/13 page no. 10 /16 language used in Section 138 (c) of NI Act clearly establishes that there has to be an actual payment of the entire cheque amount within 15 days by the accused, otherwise cause of action for filing complaint U/s 138 NI Act arises in favour of the complainant. Tendering part payment of cheque amount after receipt of notice, within 15 days, is not payment made within the meaning of Section 138 ( c) NI Act, hence, the accused can not evade prosecution even if the said part payment has been accepted by the complainant

title: A) Shankar Finance And ... vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors. on 5 July, 2014
content: within 15 days, is not payment made within the meaning of Section 138 ( c) NI Act, hence, the accused can not evade prosecution even if the said part payment has been accepted by the complainant. The same has been held by the Hon'ble Calcutta High Court in the case of M/s Ancon Engineering Co. (P) Ltd v. Amitava Goswami 1994 Crl. LJ 351. Hence, the defence of part payment raised by the accused is actually no defense and thus rejected. 18 The main contention / defense raised by the accused persons is that the present complaint is not maintainable as it has been filed by Power of Attorney holder who has not filed original Power of Attorney. Further, the accused has stated that the power of attorney holder did not have personal knowledge regarding the facts of the case and the complainant who had personal knowledge has not deposed before this Court. Therefore, the evidence of power of attorney holder can not be considered and hence, the present complaint is liable to be dismissed. 19 Although the original power of attorney has not been placed on record yet it is seen from the pre summoning evidence dated 04.07.2013 that original of Ex. CW1/A (OSR) was shown to the Court before exhibiting the photocopy on record. Further, it is also noticed that original of Ex. CW1/B (OSR) which is the minutes of the meeting dated 10.09.2010 was shown to the Court before exhibiting the photocopy on record. Therefore, the objection that the original documents have not been placed on record is without merit as the photocopies have been exhibited only CC No. 441/13 page no. 11 /16 after perusal of the originals by the Court

title: A) Shankar Finance And ... vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors. on 5 July, 2014
content: that the original documents have not been placed on record is without merit as the photocopies have been exhibited only CC No. 441/13 page no. 11 /16 after perusal of the originals by the Court. 20 In the case relied upon by the accused persons namely Shanker Finance & Investment V/s State of Andhra Pradesh (2008) 8 SCC 536, the Hon'ble Apex Court had held that the attorney holder can not file the complaint in his own name as if he was the complainant, but he can initial criminal proceedings on behalf of the principal. Hence, Ex. CW1/A (OSR), which authorizes the present authorized representative to pursue both Civil and Criminal cases arising out of unpaid invoices / bills, is sufficiently granting required authorization to the present authorized representative to pursue the present case. 21 The accused persons have argued that from the evidence of attorney holder, it is clear that he is unaware of the transaction between the parties and therefore, could not have given evidence. The accused persons have relied upon the following portions of the attorney holder's cross­examination in support of their argument: "I do not know anything outside the terms of the complaint. ...... I am not aware if after issuance of allotment letter physical possession of the shop was given to the accused persons or not. ..... I have to check the records to state what was the total payment made by the accused persons. ...... Question : I put it to you that accused persons have already paid a sum of Rs. 28,15,000/­ in respect of the allotment ? CC No. 441/13 page no. 12 /16 Ans.: I do not know I can tell only after checking the records. Question : I put it to you that after dishonor of the cheque bearing no. 154027 and 154028 amount of Rs

title: A) Shankar Finance And ... vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors. on 5 July, 2014
content: ? CC No. 441/13 page no. 12 /16 Ans.: I do not know I can tell only after checking the records. Question : I put it to you that after dishonor of the cheque bearing no. 154027 and 154028 amount of Rs. 1,00,000 was transferred in the account of the complainant company by way of RTGS on 29.05.2013. i.e. within 15 days of receiving the legal notice? Ans. : I do not about the same. I have to check the records. It is not in my knowledge if the complainant has received the reply of legal notice. ...... Question : I put to you that accused persons were not liable to pay the cheque amount i.e. Rs. 10,00,000/­ to the complainant company on the date of the cheques? Ans. They have to pay as per agreement. I personally do not know if they were liable or not." 22 It is well settled that statutory presumption regarding liability of the accused to make payment exists in favour of the complainant and the onus to rebut the same is upon the accused. As already discussed above, the accused persons have failed to rebut this presumption of their liability to pay to the complainant the cheque amount. Further, ingredients of offence u/s 138 NI Act, like the signatures on cheque, issuance of cheque to the complainant, dishonour of cheque, receipt of legal demand notice and failure to make payment of cheque amount within 15 days of receipt of legal demand notice have been proved against the accused persons. The accused persons could have raised this defense of incompetence of attorney holder to give evidence in case they had successfully rebutted the statutory presumption of liability to pay. Only then, the onus would have shifted back to the complainant to prove the liability to pay and then it would have been detrimental to their case that CC No. 441/13 page no

title: A) Shankar Finance And ... vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors. on 5 July, 2014
content: of liability to pay. Only then, the onus would have shifted back to the complainant to prove the liability to pay and then it would have been detrimental to their case that CC No. 441/13 page no. 13 /16 the attorney holder is unaware about the transaction between the parties. However, in absence of this shifting of onus upon the complainant, all the necessary ingredients for offence under section 138, NI Act stand satisfied by the present attorney holder only. Further, although the attorney holder is neither a signatory nor a witness to the agreement dated 05.03.2013, pursuant to which the cheque in question had been issued, yet, the said agreement has not been disputed by the accused persons. Therefore, the said agreement, on account of admission, stands proved and there is no need for examination of person having personal knowledge about the said agreement on behalf of the complainant. It is also to be noted that the present argument under discussion is a technical one, and in absence of rebuttal of presumption, it does not deserve to be allowed as technical considerations should not defeat substantive justice. 23 The judgments relied upon by the accused are not relevant to the facts of the present case. Shanker Finance & Investment V/s State of Andhra Pradesh (2008) 8 SCC 536, is distinguishable as the same deals with a proprietorship concern, while the present complaint has been filed by a company. Janki V. Bhojwani V/s Indusind Bank and Ors. Civil Appeal No. 6790 of 2003 decided on 06.12.2004 is distinguishable as the same is concerned with civil law and not criminal proceedings. National Small Industries Corporation Ltd. V/s State (NCT of Delhi) and Ors

title: A) Shankar Finance And ... vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors. on 5 July, 2014
content: 6790 of 2003 decided on 06.12.2004 is distinguishable as the same is concerned with civil law and not criminal proceedings. National Small Industries Corporation Ltd. V/s State (NCT of Delhi) and Ors. 2007(1) JCC 69(Delhi) deals with a complaint by government companies, while the present complaint has been filed by a private limited company. Narender Kumar V/s Harnam Singh Criminal Appeal No. 11 of 1996 decided on 25.06.1999 is not applicable to the facts of the present case because the cheque in question has admittedly been issued by the accused persons CC No. 441/13 page no. 14 /16 pursuant to the agreement dated 05.03.2013. Therefore, there is no question of the cheque not having been issued against legal liability. 24 There have been some miscellaneous arguments raised by the accused persons. One such argument raised by the accused persons is that the complainant has taken excess consideration than what was agreed in agreement dated 05.03.2013. The accused persons have submitted that the consideration as per agreement was Rs.34,50,000/­ while the complainant has already taken an amount of Rs.37,15,000/­ from the accused persons by way of cash and cheque. Therefore, the accused persons have argued that the present case is not maintainable. The accused persons have not led any evidence to prove their claim of having paid Rs. 37,15,000/­ to the complainant. The accused persons have only made bald statements in their application U/s 145(2) NI Act that the said amount had been paid. The said contentions had been reiterated in the alleged reply notice dated 15.06.2013. However, neither the said reply notice nor statement of account annexed with application U/s 145(2) NI Act have been proved by way of evidence by the accused persons

title: A) Shankar Finance And ... vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors. on 5 July, 2014
content: reply notice dated 15.06.2013. However, neither the said reply notice nor statement of account annexed with application U/s 145(2) NI Act have been proved by way of evidence by the accused persons. It is well established that statutory presumption U/s 138 NI Act exists in favour of the complainant and the onus of proving his innocence is upon the accused. Therefore the onus of proving that the accused persons have paid the agreed consideration or more is upon the accused persons. In absence of any defense evidence the same has not been proved and therefore this argument also does not merit any consideration. 25 The accused persons have further argued that the bona fides of the complainant is questionable as the complainant has deliberately suppressed the fact that they received reply notice dated 15.06.2013. It is well settled that the cause CC No. 441/13 page no. 15 /16 of action arises U/s 138 NI Act on failure of the accused to make payment within 15 days of receipt of legal demand notice and it is immaterial that the accused replied to the legal demand notice without making payment of the cheque amount. Hence, the present argument is also without any merit. 26 Considering the entire evidence on record, it stands duly proved that the cheque in question Ex. CW­1/D was issued and drawn in discharge of legal liability of the accused persons and for consideration. 27 In view of the above discussion, I am of the considered opinion that the complainant has proved the ingredients for offence u/s 138 NI Act against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt. Accordingly, accused M/s Janta Buildtech Pvt. Ltd. Alongwith its directors Sh. Ashu Gupta and Sh

title: A) Shankar Finance And ... vs State Of Andhra Pradesh And Ors. on 5 July, 2014
content: proved the ingredients for offence u/s 138 NI Act against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt. Accordingly, accused M/s Janta Buildtech Pvt. Ltd. Alongwith its directors Sh. Ashu Gupta and Sh. Vipin Tyagi, GF­01, Omaxe Park Plaza, SK­II, Indirapuram, Ghaziabad (U.P.) stand convicted of the offence under section 138 NI Act. content: Rani Page No. 13/13 entire record of the case file. Before proceeding further it is imperative for me to go through the relevant provisions of law. Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act provides that: "Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc, of funds in the account:Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in while or in part, of any debt or other liability, is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with that bank, such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall, without prejudice to any other provisions of this Act, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may be extended to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both: Provided that nothing contained in this section shall apply unless (a) the cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier; (b) the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within thirty days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid; and (c) the drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or, as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque, within fifteen days of the receipt of the

title: Cc No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj vs . Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 on 23 August, 2014
content: drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or, as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque, within fifteen days of the receipt of the said notice. Explanation:For the purposes of this section, "debt or other liability" means a legally enforceable debt or other liability. APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE IN THE LIGHT OF THE INGREDIENTS OF SECTION 138 OF THE NI ACT AND THE DEFENCE RAISED BY THE ACCUSED 7 It is not disputed by the accused that the Cheque in Question Ex. CW1/1 is drawn on the account maintained by her. Infact the accused in her statement U/s 313 of the Code has CC No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj Vs. Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 specifically admitted that the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 belongs to her, however the accused denied her signature's on the same. Further the presentation, dishonor of the cheque in question and the cheque returning memo has also not been challenged by the accused. Therefore, In light of the evidence on record coupled with the admission by the accused it stands duly proved that the cheque in question Ex CW1/1 is drawn on the account of the accused. Further it also stands proved that the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 was got dishonored vide cheque returning memo Ex. CW1/2 with the reason "Funds Insufficient". 8 From the perusal of the entire evidence it has come to fore that two fold defence has been taken by the accused. Firstly, that she has not been served with the legal demand notice by the complainant and the Secondly that she has not taken any loan from the complainant and the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 do not bears her signature and the same has not been issued by her in order to discharge her loan liability as alleged by the complainant

title: Cc No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj vs . Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 on 23 August, 2014
content: from the complainant and the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 do not bears her signature and the same has not been issued by her in order to discharge her loan liability as alleged by the complainant. 9 Coming to the first line of defence taken by the accused that she has not been served with the legal demand notice by the complainant. It is pertinent to note that the complainant Om Parkash Bhardwaj has examined himself as CW­1 and has specifically stated in his evidence affidavit Ex. CW1/A that he has got issued the legal demand notice Ex. CW1/3 to the accused through registered post and UPC. The complainant (CW­1) has not placed the postal receipts on record vide which the legal demand notice has been send to the accused however the complainant has tendered in evidence a non cognizable receipt Ex. CW1/8 in respect of the missing postal receipts. The complainant has also tendered the returned envelopes along with AD cards as Ex. CW1/4 to Ex. CW1/7. The accused Geeta Devi has denied the receipt of the legal demand notice both at the time of framing of notice U/s 251 of the Code and also in her Statement U/s CC No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj Vs. Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 313 of the Code. On perusal of the returned envelopes Ex. CW1/4 to Ex. CW1/7 it is revealed that they have been sent at all the addresses of the accused mentioned by the complainant in the complaint. The returned envelopes Ex. CW1/4 to Ex. CW1/7 also bears the postal receipt dated 12/01/2011 which is generated at time of booking a parcel by the postal authorities. Therefore there remains no doubt that the legal demand has been sent by the complainant to the accused at the address mentioned on the same. Further it is also revealed that all of them have been returned unserved

title: Cc No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj vs . Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 on 23 August, 2014
content: remains no doubt that the legal demand has been sent by the complainant to the accused at the address mentioned on the same. Further it is also revealed that all of them have been returned unserved. It is interesting to see that throughout the trial the accused has never challenged that the addresses mentioned on the legal demand notice Ex. CW1/3 or the returned envelopes Ex. CW1/4 to Ex. CW1/7 are incorrect or she was not residing at the said addresses at the time when the legal demand notice was sent to her. Further it is also surprising to see that accused has simply denied the receipt of the legal demand notice Ex. CW1/3 and has not any lead any evidence to corroborate her stand. Furthermore not even a suggestion to this effect was put to witness CW­1 (Complainant) during his cross examination by the counsel for the accused. Therefore in the absence of any contrary evidence it stands proved that the legal demand notice Ex. CW1/3 has been sent by the complainant at the correct addresses of the accused. It is trite to say that when there is service of notice by post on the correct addresses of the accused which evidently has taken place in the present case intentional non receipt of the same on the part of the accused would amount to proper service. Otherwise, a trickster cheque drawer would avoid receiving the legal demand notice by adopting different strategies and escape from legal consequences of Section 138 of the NI Act. Therefore, there is always a presumption that the legal demand notice has been duly served upon the accused unless some concrete evidence in rebuttal is adduced by the accused to establish that the Legal Demand Notice has not been served upon her which is totally absenting in the present case

title: Cc No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj vs . Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 on 23 August, 2014
content: the accused unless some concrete evidence in rebuttal is adduced by the accused to establish that the Legal Demand Notice has not been served upon her which is totally absenting in the present case. It was for the accused to rebut the presumption about the service of notice and CC No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj Vs. Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 show that she had no knowledge that the notice was brought to her address or that the address mentioned on the cover was incorrect or that the letter was never tendered or that remarks on the returned envelopes are incorrect or she was not responsible for the non service. Except denials the accused has not any lead any evidence to corroborate her stand. Therefore it stands proved that the legal demand notice Ex. CW1/3 has been served upon the accused. As such non receipt of the legal demand notice as a defence on part of the accused has no force. 10 Coming to the second line of defence taken by the accused that she has not taken any loan from the complainant and the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 does not bears her signature and the same has not been issued by her in order to discharge her loan liability as alleged by the complainant. 11 It is trite to say that the crux of penal liability under Section 138 of NI Act is that the Cheque in question must be issued for the discharge of any legal debt or liability. Existing of legal debt or liability is sine qua non for constituting the offence. 12 In the case in hand it is the case of the complainant that on 15.08.2010 the accused along with her husband has approached him for granting a loan of Rs. 20,00,000/­ lakhs stating that she is need of money for treatment of her bhabhi and a loan of Rs

title: Cc No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj vs . Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 on 23 August, 2014
content: that on 15.08.2010 the accused along with her husband has approached him for granting a loan of Rs. 20,00,000/­ lakhs stating that she is need of money for treatment of her bhabhi and a loan of Rs. 19,70,000/­ was granted by the complainant to the accused for three months and in discharge of her liability the accused has issued the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1. The accused has refuted the claim of the complainant. At the time of framing of notice under section 251 of the code the accused has stated that she has not issued that cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 to the complainant and the same does not bears her signature. Further the accused also stated that the complainant has taken the cheque in question from her by fraud. In her statement CC No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj Vs. Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 under section 313 of the code the accused again denied having taken any loan from the complainant and stated that complainant along with Rajiv Kumar had got an electricity meter installed at her house and for the same the complainant had taken her cheque book. It was also contended by the accused that the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 does not bears her signature and the complainant had misused her cheque for filing the present complaint case. 13 To corroborate her stand the accused has examined three witnesses in her defence. DW­1 Kailash Chopra, Deputy Manager, SBI Bank, Palam Colony (drawee bank), DW­2 Dr. Amulya Bharat and DW­3 handwriting expert Deepak Jain. It is not the case of the accused that the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 is not drawn on the account maintained by her. The accused has simpliciter denied her signature's on the same. Now coming to the aspect whether the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 bears the signature of the accused

title: Cc No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj vs . Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 on 23 August, 2014
content: on the account maintained by her. The accused has simpliciter denied her signature's on the same. Now coming to the aspect whether the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 bears the signature of the accused. It is trite to say that an essential feature of a cheque is that it has to be signed by the maker. The accused has denied her signature on the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 at both the stages under section 251 of the code and also in her statement under section 313 of the code. It is pertinent to note that the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 is drawn on State Bank of India and the same was deposited in the Janta Cooperative Bank in the account of the complainant. It is also pertinent to note that the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 is dishonored vide cheque returning memo Ex. CW1/2 due to "insufficient funds". It is interesting to see that the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 bounced not on account of the fact that the signature on cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 was not tallying with the specimen signature of the accused kept with the bank, but on account of 'insufficient funds'. Had the signature on cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 been different, the bank would have returned the same with the remark that the signature on the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 was not tallying with the accused specimen signature's kept with the bank. The Cheque returning memo Ex. CC No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj Vs. Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 CW1/2 issued by the bank clearly show that signature of the accused on cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 was not objected to by the bank, but the same was returned with the remark "insufficient fund". In the case of denial of signature of the drawer of a cheque, the best witness would be the concerned Bank Manager

title: Cc No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj vs . Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 on 23 August, 2014
content: to by the bank, but the same was returned with the remark "insufficient fund". In the case of denial of signature of the drawer of a cheque, the best witness would be the concerned Bank Manager. It is interesting to see that the accused has also examined the official of his bank (drawee bank) as DW­1. Now coming to the evidence of DW­1 Kailash Chopra, Deputy Manager, SBI Bank i.e. the accused bank (drawee bank). DW­1 has placed on record the statement of account of the accused as Ex. DW1/1 and has also placed on record the copy of the account opening form of the accused as Ex. DW1/2. The witness has also placed on record the photocopy of the cheque obtained for clearance from CTS as Ex. DW1/3. Perusal of the account opening form Ex. DW1/2 shows that the account on which the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 is drawn is in the joint name of the accused Geeta Devi and her husband Ashok Kumar. Surprisingly, DW­1 has not placed the complete account opening form of the accused on record and only one page is placed on record. Further DW­1 in his evidence has nowhere deposed about the fact that the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 does not bears the signature of the accused or the signatures on the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 do not tally with the signature of the accused available with the bank in records maintained by it. Furthermore, the witness has also not placed the specimen signatures of the accused on record obtained by the bank from the accused at the time of opening the account. DW­1 simpliciter has tendered the statement of the account of the accused, copy of the cheque obtained through CTS and account opening form of the accused. Further to corroborate her stand that the cheque in question Ex

title: Cc No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj vs . Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 on 23 August, 2014
content: tendered the statement of the account of the accused, copy of the cheque obtained through CTS and account opening form of the accused. Further to corroborate her stand that the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 do not bears her signature the accused has also examined handwriting expert Deepak Jain as DW­3. The said witness has placed his report Ex. DW3/A and enlarged photographs of admitted and specimen signatures as Ex. DW3/B (Colly.). Surprisingly on perusal of the report Ex. DW3/A it is revealed that the handwriting expert DW­3 has come to the conclusion that due to difference in CC No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj Vs. Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 script of the disputed signatures and the admitted signatures the opinion is not possible. It is quite surprising to see that there no plausible explanation given by handwriting expert DW­3 as what prevented him from taking the signature of accused in hindi script so as to compare it with the alleged denied signature on the cheque in question. Therefore it is evident and apparently clear that the testimonies of DW­1 and DW­3 have not at all supported the stand of the accused that the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 do not bears her signature. Therefore in view of my discussion it stands proved that the signature on cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 are that of the accused. 14 During course of arguments Ld counsel also argued that the particulars in the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 have also not been filled by the accused. It is also trite to say that once the signature on the cheque in question is proved to be that of the accused as has happened in the case in hand the plea of the accused that particulars in the cheque in question Ex

title: Cc No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj vs . Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 on 23 August, 2014
content: to say that once the signature on the cheque in question is proved to be that of the accused as has happened in the case in hand the plea of the accused that particulars in the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 has also not been filled by her are of no consequence as there is no rule of banking business that the name of the payee as well as the amount should be written by the drawer himself, as no law provides that in case of cheque the entire body has to be written by the drawer only. 15 Now coming to the evidence of DW­2 Dr. Amulya Bharat, the said witness has deposed before the court about the medical condition of one Ashok Kumar who is the husband of the accused. The witness has stated about the fact that husband of the accused is under treatment as he is suffering from Paranoid Schizophrenia. The evidence of the said witness is not at all relevant in the present proceedings as the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 is neither issued by the husband of the accused nor the same bears his signatures. Furthermore, it is not the case of the complainant that the loan amount was given to the husband of the accused or the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 has been issued by him. CC No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj Vs. Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 16 Therefore it is apparent that all the defence witnesses have not at all supported the claim of the accused. Further the accused has not even examined herself as a defence witness to corroborate her stand. Furthermore the accused have not even examined the said Rajiv Kumar in whose presence the complainant allegedly has taken her cheque book. Apart from the aforesaid vague and flawed defence, the accused has not lead any cogent evidence to corroborate her stand

title: Cc No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj vs . Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 on 23 August, 2014
content: Kumar in whose presence the complainant allegedly has taken her cheque book. Apart from the aforesaid vague and flawed defence, the accused has not lead any cogent evidence to corroborate her stand. It is trite to say that mere denial on the part of the accused would not absolve her from any liability. It was for the accused to prove the circumstances under which the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 has come in the possession of the complainant by leading cogent evidence so as to discharge and rebut the presumption raised against her by the Statute U/s 139 and 118 (a) of the NI Act and mere simplicitor denying the allegations would not be at her advantage. Further merely putting suggestions to the complainant's witness and giving explanations in the statement U/s 313 of the Code without leading any defence to corroborate the same would also not be sufficient to discharge the burden of presumptions casted upon the accused by virtue of provisions of Section 118 (a) and 139 of the NI Act. There is no presumption of law that the explanations given by the accused are truthful. Mere pleading non guilty at the stage of notice U/s 251 of the Code or explanation given in statement U/s 313 of the Code or suggestions put to the complainant in cross examination does not amount to rebuttle of the presumption U/s 139 of the NI Act. 17 The accused has not brought any material on record and also no cogent explanations or any probable defence which would re­ but the shadow of presumption existing in favour of the Complainant. This court do not find any force in the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the accused that the accused has succeeded in re­ butting the presumption under Section 139 of the Act. CC No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj Vs. Geeta Rani Page No

title: Cc No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj vs . Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 on 23 August, 2014
content: advanced by the learned counsel for the accused that the accused has succeeded in re­ butting the presumption under Section 139 of the Act. CC No. 5051/14 Om Parkash Bhardwaj Vs. Geeta Rani Page No. 13/13 18 From the materials brought on record and evidence lead by the parties it stands duly proved that the accused has failed to rebut the presumptions U/s 118 (a) and section 139 of the NI Act. Therefore, I hereby hold that the Complainant has proved and substantiated its allegations that the cheque in question Ex. CW1/1 was issued by the accused in discharge of her legal liability and for consideration. Fur­ thermore, it also stands proved that no payment has been made by the accused to the complainant within 15 days from the receipt of the le­ gal demand notice. 19 In view of the aforesaid discussion, I hereby hold that the complainant has proved and substantiated its allegation against the accused and all the ingredients of Section 138 of NI Act also stands proved. Accordingly, accused Geeta Rani W/o Sh. Ashok Kumar, is hereby convicted of the offence U/s 138 of NI Act. This Judgment contains 13 pages and every Page of this judgment has been signed by me. title: Sh. Shyam Sunder vs By Way Of The Present Judgment on 28 January, 2014
content: IN THE COURT OF SH. GAJENDER SINGH NAGAR METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE, KKD, EAST, NEW DELHI Complaint No. 38/11 Unique ID No. 02402R0163362011 PS. Preet Vihar Sh. Shyam Sunder S/o Sh. Subhash Chand, R/o H.No. 29, Gali No.29, Sarojni Park, Delhi­31 ......... Complainant. Versus Sh. Gaurav Jain, S/o Sh. Roshan Lal Jain, R/o Dhobiwali Gali, Near Civil Hospital, Rohtak (Haryana) ......... Accused. COMPLAINT U/s 138 OF THE NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS ACT Offence complained of : U/s 138 N.I. Act Date of commission of offence : 21.05.2011 Plea of Accused : Not guilty Complaint filed on : 28.05.2011 Final Arguments heard & Concluded on : 08.01.2014 Date of decision of the case : 28.01.2014 Final order : Acquittal CC No. 38/11 SHYAM SUNDER Vs. GAURAV JAIN page no. 1 /14 BRIEF FACTS AND REASONS FOR DECISION OF THE CASE 1. By way of the present judgment, this court shall decide the complaint case U/s 138 Negotiable Instrument Act 1881 (as amended up to date) filed by the complainant Sh. Shyam Sunder against the accused Gaurav Jain. 2. The prosecution story in brief necessary for the disposal of the present case is that, the accused had good friendly relations with the complainant. On 02.04.2010 accused approached the complainant and requested him to advance a friendly loan of Rs. 4,00,000/­ on that the complainant gave a loan of Rs.3,60,000/­ in cash to the accused after withdrawing the same from Central Bank of India, Patpar Ganj Road, Delhi on 06.04.2010. At the time of granting loan the accused had acknowledge the receipt of said sum of Rs.3,60,000/­. Towards discharge of the said loan, the accused issued a cheque bearing no. 449808 dated 29.04.2011 for the sum of Rs

title: Sh. Shyam Sunder vs By Way Of The Present Judgment on 28 January, 2014
content: loan the accused had acknowledge the receipt of said sum of Rs.3,60,000/­. Towards discharge of the said loan, the accused issued a cheque bearing no. 449808 dated 29.04.2011 for the sum of Rs. 3.60,000/­ drawn on PNB, Rohtak Road (Haryana) branch to the complainant but on presentation the said cheque was returned back dishonored with the remark "INSUFFICIENT FUND" vide dishonour memo dated 03.05.2011. Thereafter a legal notice was sent to the accused on 04.05.2011 by way of regd AD and UPC. It is further alleged that despite service of legal notice accused has not paid the cheque amount to the complainant till the filling of the case. 3. After the complaint was filed, summons were issued against the accused vide order dated 02.07.2011 for the offence U/s 138 CC No. 38/11 SHYAM SUNDER Vs. GAURAV JAIN page no. 2 /14 Negotiable Instrument Act 1881. On appearance of the accused notice U/s 251 Cr.P.C. dated 06.09.2011 was framed upon the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 4. In order to prove the case, the complainant examined himself as CW­1 and reiterated the contents of the complaint on oath before this court and filed an affidavit in evidence. He also exhibited original cheque bearing No.449808 as Ex. CW1/1, the cheque returning memo as Ex. CW1/2, the legal notice of demand dated 04.05.2011 is exhibited as Ex. CW1/3, The original receipts of registered post as Ex. CW1/4 & Courier receipt as Ex. CW1/5, letter issued by Senior post master as Ex. CW1/6. Thereafter, the complainant evidence was closed at request. 5. The statement of accused was recorded U/s 313 Cr.P.C in which all the incriminating evidence along with exhibited documents were put to the accused

title: Sh. Shyam Sunder vs By Way Of The Present Judgment on 28 January, 2014
content: the complainant evidence was closed at request. 5. The statement of accused was recorded U/s 313 Cr.P.C in which all the incriminating evidence along with exhibited documents were put to the accused. In his statement accused stated that he had not taken any loan of Rs.3,60,000/­ from the complainant. Infact the cheque in question was given in the year 2008 as Bayana / Advance for a property he wanted to purchase which was in the name of complainant's wife. This cheque was given along with one more cheque bearing no. 449806 of Rs. 3,00,000/­ on which he had written name of the wife of the complainant. He had also given cash of Rs.5,25,000/­ to the complainant towards agreement to sell. The accused examined himself as DW­1 and reiterated his defence as stated above. He CC No. 38/11 SHYAM SUNDER Vs. GAURAV JAIN page no. 3 /14 also exhibited agreement executed between wife of the complainant and himself as Ex. DW1/1 & Ex. DW1/2, Photocopy of Sale deed as Ex. DW1/3, Copy of complaint made by the accused against the complainant to DSP, Rohtak as Ex. DW1/4, copy of complaint made by the accused against the complainant to police as Ex. DW1/5, Invitation card as Ex. DW1/6, Press release in respect of the party issued by Mr. Sunil Jain, Director of One City Infrastructure Ltd as Ex. DW1/7, delivery challan of Bike as Ex. DW1/8, original invitation card for the inauguration party at One City, Rohtak dated 06.04.2010 as Mark DW1/X1. Ms. Rajni examined as DW­2 No other witness was examined and Defence Evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments. 6. I have heard Ld. counsels and perused the entire record of the case file and the evidence on record. Both the counsel have referred to a number of cases, I have discussed them at the relevant place. 7

title: Sh. Shyam Sunder vs By Way Of The Present Judgment on 28 January, 2014
content: have heard Ld. counsels and perused the entire record of the case file and the evidence on record. Both the counsel have referred to a number of cases, I have discussed them at the relevant place. 7. Before proceeding further let us go through the relevant provisions of law. The main ingredient of Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act are as follows:­ (a) The accused issued a cheque on an account maintained by him with a bank. (b) The said cheque has been issued in discharge of any legal debt or other liability. (c) The cheque has been presented to the bank within the CC No. 38/11 SHYAM SUNDER Vs. GAURAV JAIN page no. 4 /14 period of six months from the date of the cheque or within the period of its validity. (d) When the aforesaid cheque was presented for encashment, the same was returned unpaid/ dishonoured. (e) The Payee of the cheque issued a legal notice of demand within 30 days from the receipt of information by him from the Bank regarding the return of the cheque. (f) The Drawer of the cheque failed to make the payment within 15 days of the receipt of the aforesaid legal notice of demand. If the aforesaid ingredients are satisfied then the drawer of the cheque shall be deemed to have committed an offence punishable u/s 138 Negotiable Instruments Act. 8. Now let us deal with the each ingredient of the section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act to see whether the case against the accused has been proved or not. WHETHER THE CHEQUE IN QUESTION HAS BEEN ISSUED IN DISCHARGE OF ANY LEGAL DEBT OR OTHER LIABILITY: 9. It is submitted by the CW­1 that at the request of the accused he gave friendly loan of Rs.3,60,000/­ in cash to the accused after withdrawing the same from Central Bank of India, Patpar Ganj Road, Delhi on 06.04.2010

title: Sh. Shyam Sunder vs By Way Of The Present Judgment on 28 January, 2014
content: the CW­1 that at the request of the accused he gave friendly loan of Rs.3,60,000/­ in cash to the accused after withdrawing the same from Central Bank of India, Patpar Ganj Road, Delhi on 06.04.2010. Towards discharge of the said loan, the accused issued a cheque bearing no. 449808 dated 29.04.2011 for the sum of Rs. 3.60,000/­ drawn on PNB, Rohtak Road (Haryana) branch to the complainant which is Ex. CW1/1. CC No. 38/11 SHYAM SUNDER Vs. GAURAV JAIN page no. 5 /14 Since the cheque in question is bearing name of the complainant as payee and signatures on the cheque is admitted by the accused to be his own, hence, prima facie it is proved that cheque was issued to the complainant. 10. At this stage let us go through the relevant provisions of law. There is a presumption in favour of the complainant u/s 118 (a) Negotiable Instruments Act that until the contrary is proved, it will be presumed that every negotiable instrument was drawn for consideration and every such instrument when it has been accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred was accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred for consideration. 11. Further Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 provides that it shall be presumed until the contrary is proved that the holder of the cheque received the cheque of the nature referred in the Section 138 for the discharge in whole or in part of his debt or liability. 12. Now it will have to be examined whether the accused has rebutted the presumption as contemplated by Section 118 (b) and Section 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act. 13. It has been observed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in V.S. Yadav Vs

title: Sh. Shyam Sunder vs By Way Of The Present Judgment on 28 January, 2014
content: the accused has rebutted the presumption as contemplated by Section 118 (b) and Section 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act. 13. It has been observed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in V.S. Yadav Vs. Reena 172(2010) DLT 561 that the offence u/s 138 NI Act is a technical offence and the complainant is only supposed to prove that the cheques issued by the respondent were dishonored, his statement that cheques were issued against liability or debt is sufficient proof of the debt or liability and the CC No. 38/11 SHYAM SUNDER Vs. GAURAV JAIN page no. 6 /14 onus shifts to the respondent / accused to show the circumstances under which the cheques came to be issued and this could be proved by the respondent only by way of evidence and not by leading no evidence. 14. Therefore after the establishment of the fact that the cheque was issued by the accused and specific statement of the complainant as stated above regarding liability of the accused the burden to rebut the presumption shifted to the accused. It is established principle of law that presumption of law as raised Under sections 138 & 118 of the N.I. Act can be rebutted only by cogent evidence. In Kumar Exports V. Sharma Carpets (2009) 2 SCC 513 it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that: To rebut the statutory presumptions an accused is not expected to prove his defence beyond reasonable doubt as is expected of the complainant in a criminal trial. The accused may adduce direct evidence to prove that the note in question was not supported by consideration and that there was no debt or liability to be discharged by him

title: Sh. Shyam Sunder vs By Way Of The Present Judgment on 28 January, 2014
content: in a criminal trial. The accused may adduce direct evidence to prove that the note in question was not supported by consideration and that there was no debt or liability to be discharged by him. However, the court need not insist in every case that the accused should disprove the non­existence of consideration and debt by leading direct evidence because the existence of negative evidence is neither possible nor contemplated. CC No. 38/11 SHYAM SUNDER Vs. GAURAV JAIN page no. 7 /14 15. In the present matter the following circumstances shows that the defence of the accused is true one: i) The sum of Rs.3,60,000/­ allegedly given by the complainant to the accused was not given by way of cheque ( i.e. in contravention of Section 269 SS of Income Tax Act, wherein it is specifically laid down that if a loan is advanced which is more then Rs.20,000/­, it has to be by way of writing reflected in the books of account) rather the same was allegedly given in cash without taking any written receipt. No written document was executed in respect of the same at the time of giving the alleged loan. There is no witness of handing­over of the money by the complainant to the accused. ii) The alleged loan of Rs.3,60,000/­ has not been shown by the complainant in his ITR. As it is claimed by him that he has never filed ITR for any year despite the fact that he used to earn Rs.8,00,000/­ to Rs.10,00,000/­ in a year as commission from the property business. It is further submitted by him that he never maintained even rough record of the commission earned by him. In his cross examination dated 09.02.2012 it is submitted by him that he had also given an another loan of Rs.3,00,000/­ to the accused at a gap of 5­7 days from the loan of Rs. 3,60,000/­

title: Sh. Shyam Sunder vs By Way Of The Present Judgment on 28 January, 2014
content: by him. In his cross examination dated 09.02.2012 it is submitted by him that he had also given an another loan of Rs.3,00,000/­ to the accused at a gap of 5­7 days from the loan of Rs. 3,60,000/­. Thus the complainant is claiming that though he used to earn Rs.8,00,000/­ to Rs.10,00,000/­ per year but never filed ITR, further he gave two loans total amounting to Rs. 6,60,000/­ at a gap of 5 to 7 days to the accused in cash without CC No. 38/11 SHYAM SUNDER Vs. GAURAV JAIN page no. 8 /14 taking any receiving. These circumstances shows that the behaviour of the complainant was not of a prudent man. Hence, a reasonable doubt arises if the complainant actually had the financial capacity to give the alleged loans of Rs.3,00,000/­ & Rs. 3,60,000/­ to the accused and even if he had the capacity he had actually given such loans to the accused or not. iii) During his cross examination on 09.02.2012 it was submitted by the complainant that his wife never had any transaction with the accused, but later on, on the same day it was accepted by the complainant that a cheque of the accused bearing no.449806 of Rs.3,00,000/­ is with his wife as it was issued in her name. This inconsistency has been explained by the complainant by saying that the loan of Rs.3,00,000/­ was also given by him to the accused. The fact that there is a cheque of the accused in the name of the wife of the complainant made the story of the accused that, he had entered into an agreement to sell with the wife of the complainant probable. iv) During his cross examination it was claimed by the complainant that accused had came to Delhi to receive the sum of Rs.3,60,000/­ on 06.04.2010. it is submitted by him, " The money was handedover by me at inside the Central Bank, Geeta colony branch

title: Sh. Shyam Sunder vs By Way Of The Present Judgment on 28 January, 2014
content: complainant that accused had came to Delhi to receive the sum of Rs.3,60,000/­ on 06.04.2010. it is submitted by him, " The money was handedover by me at inside the Central Bank, Geeta colony branch. I had handedover the money to the accused prior to the lunch time inside the bank". Thus as per complainant the money was handedover by him to the accused prior to lunch time of the bank i.e. must be prior to 02:00 PM. On the other hand Counsel for the complainant had put a suggestion to the CC No. 38/11 SHYAM SUNDER Vs. GAURAV JAIN page no. 9 /14 accused in his cross examination U/s 315 Cr. PC that " Q. I put it to you that the function of One City, Rohtak was ended by 02:00 to 02:30 PM and thereafter you collected the loan amount from the complainant on the very same day i.e. 06.04.2010...?". this suggestion was denied by the accused. However, this suggestion shows that the complainant is taking shifting stands as at one point it is claimed that accused had taken the money at bank in pre lunch session on the other hand it is suggested to the accused that a function accused is claiming to be attended by him was ended by 02:00 to 02:30 PM and thereafter he came to Delhi. It take atleast three hours on a normal day to drive to Delhi from Rohtak, hence, as per the suggestion given by the Ld. Counsel for the complainant the accused might have came only at 05:00 or 05:30 PM to take the money from the complainant. Thus there is clear inconsistency in the version of the complainant. v) There is no document on record to show that accused had withdrawn the sum of Rs.3,60,000/­ from the bank on 06.04.2010. However, during final arguments Ld

title: Sh. Shyam Sunder vs By Way Of The Present Judgment on 28 January, 2014
content: in the version of the complainant. v) There is no document on record to show that accused had withdrawn the sum of Rs.3,60,000/­ from the bank on 06.04.2010. However, during final arguments Ld. counsel for the complainant has filed on record photocopy of the passbook of the complainant and his wife showing that a sum of Rs.3,60,000/­ was withdrawn on 06.04.2010 from their account. But this document has not been duly proved as per law. Hence, the same can not be relied by the Court. Further, even if it is assumed that a sum of Rs.3,60,000/­ was withdrawn by the complainant from his account that does not mean that the same must have been CC No. 38/11 SHYAM SUNDER Vs. GAURAV JAIN page no. 10 /14 handedover to the accused. vi) In the decision reported as 2006 (6) SCC 39 M.S. Narayana Menon @ Mani vs. State of Kerala & Anr., it was observed as under:­ "52. ................ If the defence is acceptable as probable the cheque therefore cannot be held to have been issued in discharge of the debt as, for example, if a cheque is issued for security or for any other purpose the same would not come within the purview of Section 138 of the Act. It has also been held by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Ravi Kumar D v. State of Delhi and anr. (Manu / DE /1538/2011) that: 9. Plain reading of the above provision of law shows that criminal liability under Section 138 NI Act is attracted only if the dishonored cheque was issued for the discharge in whole or in part of any existing debt or liability. The Section does not apply to a cheque issued to meet future liability which may arise on happening of some contingency

title: Sh. Shyam Sunder vs By Way Of The Present Judgment on 28 January, 2014
content: issued for the discharge in whole or in part of any existing debt or liability. The Section does not apply to a cheque issued to meet future liability which may arise on happening of some contingency. Thus, it is clear that a post­dated cheque, if issued for discharge of a debt due, in the event of dishonor, would attract section 138 if the NI Act but a cheque issued not for an existing debt / liability but issued by way of security for meeting some future contingency would not attract Section 138 of the NI Act. CC No. 38/11 SHYAM SUNDER Vs. GAURAV JAIN page no. 11 /14 16. From the above stated discussion it is established that complainant fails to prove that the accused was liable to pay the cheque amount to him. Complainant has not filed on record any document whatsoever to show the liability of the accused, hence, the defence of the accused that the cheque in question was given under an agreement to sell and not for discharging the loan appears to be probable. It is argued on behalf of the complainant that the accused has failed to prove execution of the agreement to sell between him and the wife of the complainant, it is also argued that the accused has failed to prove his alibi. It is established principle of law that the accused has only to create a doubt in the version of the complainant, while the complainant has to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt. In the present matter wife of the complainant has examined as DW­2. She was a housewife and she knew nothing even about ITR, infact she denied having a cheque bearing no. 449806 of the accused with herself while the complainant (her husband) has submitted that his wife is having the cheque bearing no.449806 of the accused with herself

title: Sh. Shyam Sunder vs By Way Of The Present Judgment on 28 January, 2014
content: having a cheque bearing no. 449806 of the accused with herself while the complainant (her husband) has submitted that his wife is having the cheque bearing no.449806 of the accused with herself. This shows that wife of the complainant never used to deal on her behalf rather complainant was the one who used to manage her affairs. Therefore it is quite possible that complainant had taken the Ikrarnama and receipt to his house to get the same signed from his wife and to get her thumb impression on the same, as stated by the accused. Therefore the defence of the accused appears to CC No. 38/11 SHYAM SUNDER Vs. GAURAV JAIN page no. 12 /14 be probable and the above stated contradictions as mentioned by Ld. Counsel for the complainant are not material enough to make defence of the accused improbable. In Kulvinder Singh v. Kafil Ahmed 2013(1) DCR 417 it was held by Hon'ble High Court: "The basic principle in criminal law is that the guilt of the accused must be proved beyond reasonable doubt and if there is a slightest doubt about the commission of an offence then the benefit has to occurred to him". 17. Thus from the above stated discussion it can be held that the accused has proved a probable defence. He has rebutted the presumptions U/s 118 (b) and 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act, on the other hand complainant has failed to prove liability of the accused positively. Considering the entire circumstances and evidence on record, it stands duly proved that the cheque in question was not issued and drawn in discharge of liability or a legally recoverable debt of the accused. Accordingly, accused Sh. Gaurav Jain, S/o Sh. Roshan Lal Jain, R/o Dhobiwali Gali, Near Civil Hospital, Rohtak (Haryana) stands acquitted of the offence U/s 138 Negotiable Instruments Act. 18.
